text:
Gabriel Vilardi lives in front of the net, and for most of the season the net wasn't kind. Then on Monday he scored three against Utah. He has six goals on 9.8 expected, and the gap between those numbers is the kind that closes, because the chances keep coming.

All Three Zones tracking (Corey Sznajder's) puts him at 9.4 scoring chances per 60 from the home plate in front of the net, 99th percentile among forwards. That's elite real estate. He has 19 points in 25 games, eight on the power play, and the Jets' share of expected goals is 3.5 points better with him on. Evolving-Hockey had him 34th among forwards in wins above replacement last season, a first-liner's number. Our range projects 59 to 82 points. In a season where Winnipeg is learning to win without Connor Hellebuyck, the Jets need goals from someone other than Kyle Connor and Mark Scheifele, and Vilardi is the likeliest candidate.
